stem.text: Let \( f(x) = 3 x \sqrt{x + 1} \). Write, but do not evaluate, an integral expression in terms of x that gives the length of the graph of f from \( x = 2 \) to \( x = 6 \).

worked_solution.text: By the product rule, \( f'(x) = \frac{3 \left(3 x + 2\right)}{2 \sqrt{x + 1}} \).
The length is the integral of \( \sqrt{1 + \left(f'(x)\right)^{2}} \) over the interval: \( \int_{2}^{6} \sqrt{1 + \left(\frac{3 \left(3 x + 2\right)}{2 \sqrt{x + 1}}\right)^{2}}\,dx \).

options.label: \( \int_{2}^{6} \sqrt{1 + \frac{3 \left(3 x + 2\right)}{2 \sqrt{x + 1}}}\,dx \)
options.derivation: the derivative left unsquared inside the radical

options.label: \( \int_{2}^{6} \left(1 + \left(\frac{3 \left(3 x + 2\right)}{2 \sqrt{x + 1}}\right)^{2}\right)\,dx \)
options.derivation: the square root left off the arc length integrand

options.label: \( \int_{0}^{6} \sqrt{1 + \left(\frac{3 \left(3 x + 2\right)}{2 \sqrt{x + 1}}\right)^{2}}\,dx \)
options.derivation: the lower limit taken as 0, the start of the axis, instead of the left end of the stated interval
